title: ARIA progress bars need an accessible name
summary: An element with role progressbar has no accessible name, so its value has no context. Add aria-label or aria-labeledby saying what is progressing.
problem: An element with role="progressbar" has no accessible name. Without one, assistive technology can announce a percentage-like value but not which task it belongs to, such as an upload or a checkout.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear progress with no subject, which is confusing when a page has more than one process running. They cannot tell what is loading or how much of their task is done.
steps: Find the element in the scan result.
Add aria-label with the task, such as "Uploading photos", or point aria-labeledby at a visible label.
Keep aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax up to date as progress changes.
Consider the native <progress> element, which provides this semantics without ARIA.
whyItMatters: Progress that cannot be identified leaves people unsure whether a task is working, and they may leave or repeat it. This rule maps to the WCAG requirement that non-text content has a text alternative, which is a Level A requirement.
howToCheck: Select the element in your browser's accessibility inspector and check that its Name is set. Run a screen reader and listen for the name and value together.
